purpose: Concept sheets for future Cesium 3D models

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished, wide landscape 3D object design sheet for ACORN's Cesium globe. This is concept art for future low-poly GLB models, not a screenshot or functioning app. Visual language: miniature museum objects, broad expertly crafted geometric silhouettes, lightly beveled edges, matte ivory ceramic and selectively colored stone, restrained satin metal, dark navy low-profile round pedestal disks, soft shadows, three-quarter orthographic studio views. Navy background #101923, ivory type, very fine quiet grid rules, ample breathing room, professional industrial design presentation, objects large enough to inspect. Architectural forms should be recognizable, intentionally simplified, avoid tiny illegible surface details, visual clutter, toy faces, random extra objects, spurious logos. Type impeccably set, concise labels below each model.
Title verbatim: "ACORN / RESEARCH OBJECTS". Subtitle: "Laboratories, facilities and research concepts".
Main area contains exactly 12 individually labeled object studies in a clean 4-column x 3-row grid:
1 "Laboratory": compact ivory modern research building with teal glazing, a broad skylight, and one simple thick rooftop vent.
2 "DOE National Laboratory": distinctive three-building ivory research campus, central teal entrance and dark round beamline research hall; a small simple plaque reads "DOE". This is a generic campus symbol, not an accurate facility model, no official seal, no nuclear cooling towers.
3 "Supercomputer": three graphite server cabinets with broad teal and amber indicator bands.
4 "User Facility": thick open circular accelerator ring around an ivory central instrument, accessible scientific instrument silhouette.
5 "Research Project": an open ivory folder holding three stepped teal task cards.
6 "Dataset": three stout stacked ivory database disks, teal inset band.
7 "Software": ivory upright slab with large teal angle brackets and slash, simple code icon.
8 "Publication": ivory open book with dark spine, two broad teal page lines.
9 "Research Team": three simple abstract head-and-shoulder figurines, ivory, teal and muted amber, no facial detail.
10 "Funding": ivory grant document with broad amber seal and a short stack of coin disks.
11 "Collaboration": three stout ivory nodes joined by thick teal bars in a triangle, all geometry connected.
12 "Field Site": ivory weather sensor mast and compact teal-roofed field station on a low earth patch.
Maintain consistent scale, teal scientific accents. Below the grid add a narrow separate strip: left a small night-Earth curved surface with three ivory miniature labs attached vertically to the local surface and teal locator rings, middle a close-up laboratory showing a green selection ring, right a tiny legend "Far: marker / Near: miniature / Selected: label". This is an illustrative zoom hierarchy, not a geographic accuracy diagram.

Title verbatim: "ACORN / U.S. LANDMARKS". Subtitle: "Recognizable silhouettes for a globe-scale collection".
Exactly eight large miniature landmark models, 4 columns x 2 rows, with these labels and designs:
"Statue of Liberty" oxidized copper green statue with raised torch and crown, on pale square plinth.
"Golden Gate Bridge" vermilion bridge with two towers, thickened simplified cables, short blue water base.
"U.S. Capitol" pale dome, broad steps and two wings, simplified classical architecture.
"Gateway Arch" elegant thick brushed-metal arch with open center.
"Grand Canyon" small terracotta stratified canyon terrain tile with a visible winding blue river, no buildings.
"Yellowstone" compact pale mineral basin with turquoise center, orange outer ring, one stout ivory geyser plume to the side.
"Kennedy Space Center" ivory rocket beside a simplified gantry, restrained amber launchpad, no logos.
"Hoover Dam" curved ivory dam between two reddish cliffs with blue water behind it.
Give each piece enough empty space and full visibility; architectural objects on dark low round disks, landscape tiles seated on the same disk family. Bottom strip a small dark globe crop of North America with only 3 enlarged landmark silhouettes and restrained pin connectors, geographic placement approximate and no label map claims. Footer exact: "Illustrative miniatures / Not to geographic scale".

Title verbatim: "ACORN / EIGHT WORLD WONDERS". Subtitle: "New Seven Wonders + Great Pyramid of Giza".
Exactly eight large miniature models, 4 columns x 2 rows. Labels below:
"Great Wall": two square watchtowers connected by a winding thick stone wall along small jade hills.
"Petra": rose sandstone cliff facade with simple carved column and pediment relief, warm red stone.
"Christ the Redeemer": pale statue with outstretched thick horizontal arms, simple robe, on compact green hill.
"Machu Picchu": pale stone terrace structures on stepped emerald mountains, iconic taller peak behind.
"Chichen Itza": warm ivory stepped pyramid, broad central stair, square summit temple.
"Colosseum": warm ivory elliptical amphitheater with simplified three tiers of arches and recognizable partially broken outer wall.
"Taj Mahal": pale ivory symmetrical mausoleum with central onion dome and four minarets surrounding it, small teal reflecting pool.
"Great Pyramid of Giza": one dominant warm sand-colored square pyramid with subtle limestone bands and two much smaller companions.
Each object rests on the same low navy round pedestal, shapes robust enough for small globe icons, identifiable by silhouette rather than texture. No mixing of landmarks. Avoid duplicate buildings or a ninth wonder. Footer exact: "One collection / Eight distinct silhouettes".

Create a distinct game-piece design board.
Title verbatim: "RISK / GLOBE PIECES". Subtitle: "Original miniatures for play on a curved world".
Composition: left 55 percent contains studio object studies, right 45 percent one dramatic but legible Cesium-like globe gameplay concept.
Top left row three LARGE original classic-style miniatures in matte ivory with blue round bases and embossed numeral plaques:
"Infantry / 1": stylized standing helmeted infantry figure carrying a short lowered rifle; broad connected silhouette, no facial details.
"Cavalry / 5": simplified horse and rider, strong solid connection between horse legs and base.
"Artillery / 10": short thick cannon on a two-wheel carriage, wide stable base.
Second left row smaller modern abstract alternative trio in same base system:
"Scout / 1": one tall beveled obelisk with single notch.
"Squadron / 5": chunky split-top rook-like tower with two notches.
"Legion / 10": low broad hexagonal fortress with three notches.
Bottom left six low faction bases in blue, orange, teal, magenta, ivory and yellow, each with a different clearly embossed symbol: circle, triangle, diamond, square, plus, star. Label "Color + symbol".
Right: beautifully rendered dark blue Earth hemisphere with generalized board-game territories drawn as restrained fine pale boundaries (not real country borders, no geographic labels), translucent blue and orange territory fills, several original ivory infantry/cavalry/cannon tokens tangent to globe surface with matching colored bases. One selected base has a white double ring. Separate readable floating army count badges "12", "7", "4". One graceful gold attack arc between nearby territories. A small inset at bottom right shows selected and unselected bases side-by-side labeled "Selected" and "Idle".
Footer exact: "Territory counts stay readable at every zoom". No dice, no extra game rules, no official Risk logo, no recreation of existing commercial sculpt designs.
